# Every command resolves its arguments the same way, through resolveUnits:
#
#   - a file named on the command line is its own unit;
#   - a directory is a package, read as one;
#   - a directory whose files declare more than one `component main` is a
#     collection of programs, and each file is its own unit.
#
# They used to each decide for themselves. `sngl generate` merged a file's
# siblings, `sngl test` deliberately never did, and `sngl check` read every
# file alone -- so the same package was one program to one command and a pile
# of undefined names to the next.

# A package: main is in app.sngl, the test that drives it is in app_test.sngl,
# and the helper it calls is in a third file.
sngl check app/
stdout 'app/app.sngl: ok'
stdout 'app/app_test.sngl: ok'

sngl test app/
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out app/
grep 'twice: 14' out/index.html

# The same directory named as one file is that file alone, which is what a
# corpus of one-file programs relies on -- and what makes naming a file mean
# "this file".
! sngl check app/app_test.sngl
stderr 'unknown type "main"'

# A directory holding several programs is not a package. Read as one it would
# report every main after the first as a duplicate; read as a corpus, each file
# stands alone.
sngl check corpus/
stdout 'corpus/one.sngl: ok'
stdout 'corpus/two.sngl: ok'

sngl test corpus/
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app/app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import app "sngl:app"

component main ui {
    var n = 7
    text #out(value="twice: {twice(n)}")
}

app.window {
    main
}
-- app/helper.sngl --
func twice(n int) => n * 2
-- app/app_test.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"

func testHelper(t Test) {
    t.assert(twice(3) == 6)
}

// `main` is declared in app.sngl, the file next to this one.
func testComponent(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.out.value == "twice: 14")
}
-- corpus/one.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import app "sngl:app"

component main ui {
    var a = 1
    text(value=string(a))
}

func testOne(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.a == 1)
}

app.window {
    main
}
-- corpus/two.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import app "sngl:app"

component main ui {
    var b = 2
    text(value=string(b))
}

func testTwo(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.b == 2)
}

app.window {
    main
}
